form.discardBody: Unsaved changes to this connection will be lost.
form.errPickAccount: Pick the {vendor} cloud account this connection should use.
form.errAccountUser: Account identifier and username are required.
form.errAws: AWS region and secret name are required.
form.errCa: Choose a CA certificate file, or pick a different SSL mode.
form.errTunnel: Choose a saved tunnel, or create one.
form.importAsk: Already saved this database in DBeaver, DataGrip, pgAdmin or another tool?
form.label: Label
form.pineconeHint: The connection is a Pinecone project, authenticated by its API key. Indexes are discovered automatically and shown as tables; query them with SQL (a WHERE metadata filter, transcribed) or a native Pinecone query.
form.noAccount: There is no {vendor} account saved yet. Add one under Settings, Cloud accounts, and it will serve this connection and your data flows alike.
form.telemetryBounded: Every query is bounded by a time range, and one that names none covers the last hour.
form.telemetryGroupSource: A GROUP BY is run by {label} itself; the results footer says what it scanned.
form.telemetryGroupHere: {label} cannot group at the source, so a GROUP BY is computed here over the events in the range.
form.snowflakeHint: Snowflake is reached over HTTPS by account identifier (no host/port or SSH tunnel). A running warehouse is needed to run queries. Password auth only for now (key-pair / SSO are not yet supported).
form.mongoUriHint: A full "mongodb://" URI (may include credentials, database, and options). A password in it is kept in the keychain when you save, and the connection string is saved without it. Over an SSH tunnel use an explicit host:port (not "mongodb+srv://"); the tunnel forces a direct single-host connection, so "replicaSet" is ignored. For Amazon DocumentDB add "?authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-1". The Username below is used only when the URI carries no user name; the Password is used either way.
form.passwordMoved: This edit changes where the connection goes or who it signs in as, so the saved password will not be sent there. Type it again to keep one.
form.sslRdsHint: For AWS RDS / Aurora endpoints: verifies the server against Amazon's RDS root CA, which isn't in the system trust store.
form.sslSystemHint: For servers whose certificate is signed by a publicly trusted CA already in the OS/Node trust store.
form.sslCustomHint: Verifies the server against a CA certificate you supply (PEM).
form.sslInsecureHint: Encrypts the connection but does not verify the server certificate. Use only when you can't supply the right CA.
form.readOnlyTitle: Block writes / DDL and disable in-grid editing for this connection.
form.readOnlyChecked: Each statement is checked before it runs.
form.dataAccess: What the AI may see of this database
form.dataAccessDefault: Use the default from AI settings
form.dataAccessOverride: Overrides the default for this database, for the assistant and coding agents.
form.dataAccessHint: Set one here to give this database its own level, for example schema only on production.
form.poolHint: Max simultaneous queries this connection runs against the database ({min} to {max}, default {def}). Raise it for heavy dashboards or parallel workloads. The database server's own connection limit still applies.
form.awsFetchTitle: Fetch the database username and password from AWS Secrets Manager at connect time instead of storing a password locally.
form.awsFetch: Fetch credentials from AWS Secrets Manager
form.awsHint: Leave the access key blank to use the named profile or your machine's default AWS credentials (env vars, SSO, instance role). The secret must be JSON with at least "username" and "password". When it carries "host" and "port" (as RDS-managed secrets do), that is where the credentials go: leave the host blank on the General tab, or give the same one, since a different host is refused. "dbname" fills in a blank database.
form.tunnelInline: Configure a tunnel for this connection
form.noTunnels: No saved tunnels yet. Create one to reuse it across connections.
form.tunnelsShared: Saved tunnels are shared: editing one updates every connection that uses it.

cloudwatch.scopesPlaceholder: optional, one per line. Leave empty to show every log group in the region.
cloudwatch.listingHint: Listing log groups is its own permission, and a credential scoped to particular ones is refused it. Name them here and the app stops asking for the list: it reads only what you named, with only the permission you already have.
cloudwatch.eachHint: Each log group in this region is shown as a table you can query with SQL:

azureMonitor.eachHint: Each table in this workspace ID is shown as a table you can query with SQL:

ssh.keepAliveTitle: Send SSH keepalives so the bastion doesn't idle-out the tunnel. Leave on unless a bastion rejects keepalive traffic.
ssh.forgetKeyHint: The app remembers the SSH server's host key the first time it connects and refuses a different one. Turn this on only if the server was rebuilt and you have confirmed its new key. After a Test or Save with this on, the next connection trusts the key it sees.

import.title: Import connections
import.intro: Choose a tool to import saved connections from. Saved usernames and passwords are imported when available; otherwise you set them after.
import.findHint: Look everywhere at once: the tools below, containers, and databases running on this computer.
import.noteCloud: These are your own hosted databases, so the username and password come with them and are kept {place}. Each one becomes an ordinary connection: importing again later picks up a reset password without making a second copy.
import.noteDbeaver: Usernames and passwords are imported from DBeaver when it has them saved (Community Edition). A connection protected by a DBeaver master password, or from DBeaver Enterprise, comes in without credentials, set those after import.
import.notePasswords: Usernames and passwords are imported from {name}; the passwords are kept {place}.
import.noteNoPasswords: Usernames are imported from {name}. Passwords are not (they're kept in your OS keychain or encrypted), so set those after import.
import.browseTitle: Import from a different config file
import.credentialsTitle: Username and password will be imported
import.unconfirmedTitle: The port is open but did not say what it is

discovery.timeout: The search did not finish within a minute.
discovery.title: Find your databases
discovery.intro: SnoutData Studio can look on this computer for databases and for connections saved in other tools. Nothing leaves this computer.
discovery.networkHint: This checks the machines on your local network for open database ports. A company's security tools can flag that, so leave it off on a work network.
discovery.empty: Nothing turned up on this computer. You can add a connection by hand, or look again later with Find Databases in the command palette or the Import connections screen.
discovery.emptyNetwork: Nothing turned up on this computer or your local network. You can add a connection by hand, or look again later with Find Databases in the command palette or the Import connections screen.

tunnels.deleteBody: Connections that use this tunnel will stop connecting until you point them at another one.
tunnels.title: SSH Tunnels
tunnels.intro: Reusable tunnels you can point many connections at. Editing one updates every connection that uses it.
tunnels.required: Name, host and username are required.
tunnels.name: Name

secretsPlace.file: in a file on this computer that only your user account can read
